page: Amazon Web Services c3.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It operates at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz and includes 25 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 15.0 GB of memory, yielding 1.88 GB per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The instance runs on the Xen hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 6681.49 and a Passmark CPU score of 7237.82. However, single-core performance is weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1280.58 and a Geekbench single-core score of 717.0. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 388.0 GB/sec for cached reads and 50.08 GB/sec for uncached reads. Cryptographic performance is average, with a Passmark encryption score of 3085.53, aided by hardware AES support. Software compilation with Clang shows average performance at 6523.0, while text processing and compression tasks are weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3.2xlarge offers a balanced profile for legacy compute-heavy workloads that benefit from dedicated vCPUs and local NVMe SSD storage without requiring modern instruction sets like AVX-512. The lack of GPU acceleration and the modest memory-to-vCPU ratio make it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale AI training. It is best suited for static web serving, software compilation, moderate database operations, and multi-threaded utility workloads that can leverage its local NVMe storage and average multi-core processing capabilities.
description: Amazon Web Services c3.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 4 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and Xen hypervisor, it includes 15.0 GB of memory and 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Performance benchmarks show average multi-core capabilities, with a Passmark CPU score of 7237.82 and a static web serving throughput of 6.84 GB/sec, though single-core performance remains weak. The instance lacks GPU acceleration and modern AVX-512 instructions. It is qualitatively cost-effective for legacy multi-threaded applications, software compilation, and static web serving that require dedicated compute resources and fast local storage without massive memory demands.
